paper-machine-learning-ultra-high-2026.summary: This is a review article surveying machine learning applications across the multiscale characterization, design, and performance prediction of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC), discussing challenges such as data scarcity and prospects for future research. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, likely in the context of addressing limited experimental data through synthetic data generation, but the evidence gives no detail on any actual use of the library.

paper-multimodal-ndt-integrated-neural-2.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal artificial neural network that fuses material, environmental, and non-destructive-testing features to predict reinforcement corrosion severity in reinforced concrete structures, using a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to augment scarce corrosion data. The augmented model reportedly achieves strong predictive accuracy (RMSE 3.55, R² 0.96) using only 30% real data, supporting condition-based maintenance decisions. The work cites the CTGAN paper in connection with its conditional GAN-based data augmentation approach, but it is unclear from the available evidence whether the SDV CTGAN implementation was actually run.

paper-synthcraft-partner-synthetic-gener.summary: This paper presents SynthCraft, an AI tool that couples a reinforcement-learning reasoning engine with large language models to let users generate and evaluate synthetic data through natural-language interaction, without requiring coding. The authors demonstrate the tool on NHANES (tabular) and TCGA (genomic) datasets, comparing privacy, statistical fidelity, and downstream utility across four generators, and show a data-augmentation workflow aimed at mitigating ethnic-group imbalance. CTGAN is run through the SynthCraft platform as one of four synthetic data generators (alongside PATE-GAN, ADS-GAN and DDPM) evaluated on both datasets, so SDV's conditional tabular GAN is used as one generator among several rather than the sole or modified model.

paper-synthetic-generation-tertiary-2026.summary: This is a tertiary study (a systematic review of secondary studies/surveys) on synthetic data generation, screening four scholarly databases from 2015-2025 and appraising 17 eligible surveys via PRISMA and DARE-4 criteria. It finds heavy concentration in healthcare, inconsistent evaluation reporting, and low reproducibility, proposing a domain-agnostic evaluation baseline. CTGAN is cited among the synthetic data generation methods referenced in the surveyed literature, but no SDV component appears to be run or evaluated directly.

paper-synthetic-combinatorial-optimizati.summary: This paper introduces DISCO (Discrete Intersection Synthesizer through Combinatorial Optimization), a novel non-neural tabular synthetic data generator that models pairwise probability intersections to reproduce marginal and pairwise distributions of an original dataset. It evaluates DISCO against several deep-learning and traditional synthesizers on synthetic and real-world datasets across regression and classification tasks, measuring statistical fidelity and ML efficacy. The evaluation is built entirely on the SDV suite: CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN and GaussianCopula are run as comparison synthesizers, SDMetrics computes the quality scores, and SDGym structures the benchmark, making SDV the empirical backbone against which DISCO is judged.

paper-synthetic-estimate-true-error-2026.summary: This paper develops generalization bounds and a method (OSYN) for estimating a trained model's true test error from synthetic data when labeled test data is scarce, validated on simulated and tabular datasets. To study how generator quality and type affect estimation accuracy, the authors compare four table generators—CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN, and Gaussian Copula—'all implemented by the open-source SDV Python package.' SDV's synthesizers are run as evaluation-subject generators across multiple experiments (Tables 5, 6, and appendix results) rather than as the paper's own proposed method.

paper-hepatitis-c-noninvasive-2025.summary: Builds non-invasive multiclass hepatitis C classification from standard laboratory panels, aimed at low-resource settings where the conventional diagnostic path is invasive and expensive. SDV-based oversampling balances the dataset before feature selection, so the library sits at the head of a pipeline intended for deployment rather than publication.

paper-athlete-performance-attenuation-20.summary: Models attenuation in athlete performance from a dataset too small and too privacy-bound to share, and rebuilds it synthetically so the modelling can proceed. The generator is TVAE run from SDV 1.17.4 with enforce_min_max_values and enforce_rounding set, and the configuration was chosen by iterating against SDMetrics' quality report; the Single Table Quality Report also backs the final fidelity claim alongside Hellinger distance. Both halves of the paper are SDV — the synthesizer and the metric that accepts it.

paper-variational-autoencoder-neural-net.summary: This paper presents a synthetic data generation approach combining a variational autoencoder and a neural network to produce synthetic recreational-runner data from baseline measurements and training responses collected over a three-month period. The synthetic data is evaluated by training predictive models on it and comparing performance, statistical similarity, and privacy metrics against models trained on real data. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) foundational paper is cited as prior work in the synthetic data generation literature.

paper-augmenting-small-tabular-health-20.summary: This paper evaluates data augmentation with generative models for small tabular health datasets, using 13 large health datasets in a simulation and seven small real datasets as an illustrative application, comparing four synthetic-data generation methods (sequential decision trees, Bayesian networks, CTGAN, and TVAE) against resampling for improving downstream gradient-boosted classifier performance. CTGAN and TVAE are run directly as two of the four generative models producing the augmented datasets reported in the results tables (e.g. Breast Cancer via CTGAN, Danish Colorectal Cancer Group via TVAE). CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional design, and TVAE, both cited to the CTGAN paper, are used as generators in the empirical evaluation, one of several methods tested rather than the sole focus.

paper-bibliometric-analysis-artificial-i.summary: A bibliometric review mapping the growth of AI-driven research on waste-to-syngas gasification, based on Scopus and Web of Science data, identifying trends such as dominance of Chinese output, focus on hydrogen-yield prediction via neural networks, and gaps in real-time control and industrial-scale validation. The paper's reference list includes the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, apparently as one of the AI methods surveyed in the literature rather than a tool the authors run. CTGAN is only cited among the AI techniques discussed in this bibliometric landscape.

paper-lime-correlation-aware-locally-202.summary: This paper proposes CO-LIME, a variant of the LIME explanation method that generates correlation-aware perturbation samples instead of assuming feature independence. It integrates a Conditional Tabular GAN into the LIME pipeline to learn feature dependencies and produce perturbation samples near the instance being explained, evaluating the approach with R2, MAE, MSE, and MedAE against baseline LIME. CTGAN is used as the perturbation-sample generator at the core of the proposed method, though the evidence does not indicate whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was run.

paper-ctgan-bandit-verification-2025.summary: Targets constrained random verification in ASIC design flow, where parametrised tests are simulated repeatedly to reach untried execution paths. CTGAN is conditioned by an Upper Confidence Bound acquisition function so generation is steered toward unexplored coverage, another instance of SDV generating a search rather than a dataset, this time from a memory manufacturer.

paper-comprehensive-review-privacy-utili.summary: A literature review surveying disclosure-limiting and synthetic data generation techniques, covering their privacy, utility, and fairness properties across statistical, copula-based, and GAN-based methods, and comparing validation and evaluation methodologies from prior studies. The paper discusses Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as a copula-based tabular synthesizer among the generators it reviews, describing its algorithm and citing other studies' comparisons of SDV against DataSynthesizer and SynthPop, without running any experiments itself. SDV's copula-based synthesizer is described in prose and cited as prior work discussed within secondary studies, but never executed by the authors.

paper-augmentation-parameter-prediction-.summary: This conference paper proposes a data augmentation and parameter prediction pipeline for chemical oxidation of aviation parts, using CTABGAN to generate synthetic samples that address hybrid imbalanced continuous/categorical process data, then feeding original plus augmented data into a gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) model for parameter prediction. The empirical work is built entirely on CTABGAN (Zhao et al.), a CTGAN descendant, described with its own mode-specific normalization and extended conditional vector design, and validated on a proprietary aviation chemical oxidation dataset. CTGAN is cited only briefly and jointly with other references as prior GAN-based work whose limitations on mixed imbalanced data motivate the choice of CTABGAN, without any indication that SDV's CTGAN itself was run.

paper-digital-twins-healthcare-review-20.summary: A survey of AI-powered digital twin applications across healthcare domains such as cardiology, diabetes, mental health, and respiratory care, cataloguing 17 distinct applications from the past four years and their generative-AI underpinnings. In describing a digital-twin-for-stress-management (DTSM) system reviewed in the survey, the authors note it integrates several tabular synthetic data generators, naming CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, REaLTabFormer and GReaT among the techniques used to preserve privacy while simulating realistic patient data. CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula (via the SDV paper) are only named as components of a third-party system being reviewed, not run by the survey's own authors.

paper-e2etune-end-end-knob-2025.summary: E2ETune is a database knob-tuning system that fine-tunes a generative language model to map workloads directly to promising configurations, avoiding the costly iterative workload-replay loop of Bayesian optimization or reinforcement-learning-based tuners. The paper introduces a data generation framework to efficiently produce workload-configuration training pairs, and shows large speedups over state-of-the-art tuners on 10 benchmark and 3 real-world workloads. The Synthetic Data Vault paper appears only in the reference list and is never discussed or used in the text.

paper-evaluatology-driven-artificial-int.summary: This paper proposes 'evaluatology', a reframing of AI evaluation as inference of how evaluation conditions causally shape outcomes, and outlines an evaluatology-based paradigm spanning data generation, training, and evaluation across the AI lifecycle. It argues for constructing causal, condition-aware training data to improve interpretability and reduce reliance on brute-force data volume. CTGAN is cited among prior work, with no indication from the available evidence that it is run or engaged with beyond citation.

paper-generating-realistic-passenger-nam.summary: This work-in-progress paper proposes a methodology for generating synthetic Passenger Name Record (PNR) data that reconstructs passenger social networks, models travel behaviours, and preserves individual-level travel histories using agent-based modelling, aiming to give security researchers a privacy-preserving alternative to restricted real PNR data. In its related-work discussion the authors describe how the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) 'provides various synthesisers, such as Gaussian Copula and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), to model data distributions' as one existing microdata-synthesis approach, without running SDV in their own pipeline. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is cited and described as prior art, not executed as part of this paper's own agent-based generation methodology.

paper-flood-probability-mapping-2025.summary: Produces high-resolution flood probability maps without the historical record or the physics simulation runs such maps normally require, both of which are limiting for most catchments. CTGAN conditionally generates synthetic precipitation point clouds that stand in for the missing events, an unusually spatial application of SDV's conditional sampling.

paper-ppia-mtl-efficient-property-2025.summary: This paper proposes PPIA-MTL, a multi-task-learning attack framework that efficiently infers proportions of sensitive attributes (binary and continuous) from tabular generative models, introducing a new evaluation metric (CACRS) and using the framework as a privacy-auditing tool across diffusion and GAN-based synthesizers. CTGAN is one of five tabular generative models attacked, with 50,000 synthetic records generated per model on Adult and Census datasets and its inference-resistance results compared against GReat, TabDDPM, TabRep, and TabSyn. SDV's CTGAN, described as introducing conditional sampling and mode-specific normalization, is run directly as one of several evaluation-subject generators.

paper-privacy-preserving-tabular-generat.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid diffusion model for generating privacy-preserving tabular data, combining differential privacy mechanisms with Gaussian diffusion for numerical attributes and multinomial diffusion for categorical attributes. It evaluates the approach on six public datasets against data utility and privacy metrics, comparing against existing tabular synthesis baselines and the state-of-the-art TabDDPM diffusion model. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators in the empirical comparison, with results reported in a data-utility table alongside the authors' own diffusion-based method.

paper-samplellm-optimizing-tabular-synth.summary: This paper proposes SampleLLM, a two-stage LLM-based framework for synthesizing tabular data for recommendation tasks, using chain-of-thought prompting and diverse exemplars followed by feature-attribution-based importance sampling to align synthetic data with the target distribution. It benchmarks against multiple tabular synthesizers (CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, GAN-based and LLM-based baselines) across recommendation and general datasets, and evaluates outputs using an 'SDV similarity' score based on column shapes and pair trends. SDV is cited as an early probabilistic tabular synthesis approach and its similarity metric is computed as an evaluation tool, while CTGAN's conditional generator and TVAE are run as comparison baselines among several generators.

paper-synthetic-generation-binary-multi-.summary: This study investigates synthetic data generation methods for binary and multi-class classification tasks in healthcare, addressing privacy, imbalance, and regulatory barriers to data access. The authors implement the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework and select its Gaussian Copula Synthesizer over CopulaGAN for its stronger statistical grounding and lower computational cost, using it to generate synthetic datasets from an imbalanced 2125-case health dataset and evaluating downstream classifier performance. SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer is run as the core generator underpinning the paper's entire synthetic data pipeline.

paper-synthetic-user-behavior-sequence-2.summary: This paper proposes IoTGen, an LLM-based framework for generating synthetic IoT user behavior sequences to retrain smart home intelligent models, including a Structure Pattern Perception Compression method to reduce token consumption during data generation. The framework addresses the staleness and privacy limitations of fixed, pre-collected smart home datasets by using LLMs to synthesize adaptive training data. SDV's original DSAA paper is cited only as one of several prior works on packet/sequence-level synthetic data generation, with no SDV code or model run.

paper-transformer-conditional-generative.summary: This paper proposes TCGANTLN, a Transformer-based conditional GAN combined with a transfer-learning network for cross-domain rolling-bearing fault diagnosis under limited data, using an expectation-maximization-based 'generation-transfer' co-training strategy. It is evaluated against several comparison generators (TTS-GAN, CorGAN, WGAN-GP, DGTL-Net, CTGAN) on CWRU and a self-made KUST-SY bearing dataset using wavelet coherence, Inception Time Score, and downstream classification accuracy. CTGAN, described as introducing 'a conditional generator... to deal with unbalanced discrete sequences', is reimplemented for bearing vibration signal data and run as one of several rejected baseline generators.

paper-clustering-resampling-technique-cl.summary: This paper proposes a clustering-based resampling technique that analyzes cluster structure to address class imbalance in software defect prediction datasets. It contributes a new oversampling strategy aimed at improving defect detection accuracy in imbalanced software engineering data. The work cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, apparently as related work on synthetic oversampling methods, though no details of its use are available in the evidence.

paper-driven-framework-enhancing-resilie.summary: This paper proposes a resilience-enhancement framework for machine-learning-based wireless propagation models used in Digital Twins, combining GAN-based tabular data augmentation with an 'Attention through Segmentation' training strategy that partitions the feature histogram into simpler sub-models. The augmentation module explicitly uses the CTGAN implementation from the SDV library, which the authors modify by initializing it with weights from a pre-trained DNN and by adding an iterative conditioning scheme to better balance under-represented histogram bins. CTGAN, sourced from SDV, is thus the core generator whose conditional sampling drives the model's data-augmentation module, and the authors build modifications on top of it.

paper-imputation-methods-comparison-2024.summary: Benchmarks classical against modern imputation on numeric data, arguing the two families are rarely compared on equal terms. The Gaussian Copula Imputer is one of the compared methods, an unusual appearance of SDV's copula in a missing-value role rather than a generation one.

paper-challenges-opportunities-generativ.summary: This study systematically benchmarks deep generative models against traditional tabular-data synthesis methods such as SMOTE and its variants, also examining post-processing techniques, to identify strengths and limitations for practical use. The evaluation finds SMOTE-family methods outperform deep generative models on small datasets, while ensembles of deep generative models with post-processing do better on large datasets. CTGAN is cited as one of the deep generative models included among the compared tabular synthesis methods.

paper-etgan-hybrid-gan-ensemble-2024.summary: This paper proposes ETGAN, a novel GAN-Transformer hybrid architecture designed to jointly generate static and time-dependent (time-series) tabular data, addressing a gap where prior generative models specialize in only one data type. The authors combine a Transformer for temporal/positional encoding with an MLP-based GAN for static features, evaluating on enterprise-style datasets including energy consumption, retail sales, and appliance energy data. CTGAN is discussed in related work as a notable prior architecture, with its conditional vector approach described as guiding generator/discriminator behavior, but it is not run or benchmarked experimentally in this paper.

paper-gan-generating-synthetic-medical-2.summary: This paper proposes a modified GAN architecture with a custom loss function that generates synthetic medical tabular data directly from statistical summaries rather than from access to real training data, evaluated on fidelity and utility metrics. The authors benchmark their proposed method against Gaussian Multivariate, SDV, and CTGAN baselines across statistical similarity tests (t-test, chi-square, Wasserstein distance) and TSTR/TRTR machine-learning utility experiments on a medical dataset. SDV and CTGAN are run as comparison baselines throughout the empirical evaluation, with SDV's synthesizer generating one of the reference synthetic datasets against which the proposed model is judged.

paper-gqeo-nearest-neighbor-graph-2024.summary: This paper proposes GQEO, a nearest-neighbor graph-based oversampling method for handling class imbalance in classification tasks, using geometric quadrilateral elements to generate synthetic minority-class samples. It is positioned within the broader oversampling literature, of which GAN-based synthetic data generation is one strand. The evidence shows only that the paper cites the CTGAN paper, with no indication CTGAN was run or compared against.

paper-gemsyd-generic-framework-synthetic.summary: This paper proposes GeMSyD, a generic methodology for building synthetic data generation frameworks, and instantiates it for event-based smart-device interaction data, using the resulting synthetic datasets to train and evaluate a neural-network prediction model. The related-work section discusses prior studies comparing synthetic data generators, noting one that analyzed systems including the Synthetic Data Vault. SDV is mentioned only as a system referenced in a discussion of related work, not run in the paper's own experiments.

paper-generating-synthetic-complicated-k.summary: This paper argues that producing high-quality synthetic data requires deep knowledge of both the source dataset and the chosen synthetic data generator, not just running an off-the-shelf tool. Using the SD2011 survey dataset, the authors compare CTGAN, DataSynthesizer, and synthpop, showing how data pre-processing choices and generator-specific hyperparameters (batch size, training steps, network architecture) dramatically affect utility as measured by pMSE and run-time. CTGAN, explicitly identified as part of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package, is run as one of three generators evaluated, with its hyperparameters tuned and its GAN-based approach discussed as a source of utility limitations.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-sy.summary: This paper explores using generative adversarial networks to synthesize a small, inconsistent stock-market dataset in finance, evaluating the generated data's statistical similarity and quality to the original via mean, similarity, and correlation measures. The authors build their own GAN-based approach for this task rather than using an existing tabular synthesis library. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run in the study.

paper-impact-augmentation-smote-gan-2024.summary: This paper addresses class imbalance in a custom VANET routing dataset built from OMNeT++/SUMO/Veins simulations, comparing SMOTE and CTGAN (and their combination) as data-augmentation strategies before training neural networks tuned with Hyperband and L1-regularized feature selection. The authors find SMOTE outperforms CTGAN and that combining SMOTE with CTGAN degrades results, using t-SNE to show CTGAN-generated samples fail to preserve class separation. CTGAN is run directly, with stated training hyperparameters (batch size, generator/discriminator learning rate), as one of the two main data-augmentation techniques evaluated against each other.

paper-mbbfauth-multimodal-behavioral-bio.summary: This paper proposes a continuous authentication system that fuses contextual, mouse, and information-interaction behavior modalities collected from a self-built website, using an LSTM-based autoencoder for per-modality anomaly detection and a stacked-generalization meta-model for decision-level fusion. To address misalignment between the three behavioral modalities, the authors employ an 'improved CTGAN' that is instantiated with a metadata object and explicit sample-order constraints to generate aligned synthetic samples. SDV's CTGAN synthesizer (with its Metadata and Constraints API) is run as the data-augmentation component whose output underlies the modality-alignment step central to the whole system.

paper-mediclass-optimized-random-forest-.summary: This paper proposes MediClass-RF, a Random Forest-based framework for classifying medicinal versus non-medicinal plants using TF-IDF textual features, augmented with artificially added synthetic-label noise to simulate real-world data quality and reporting 89% accuracy with feature-importance analysis. In its introduction it describes Gaussian Copula models as a synthetic data generation technique used to enhance small datasets by estimating the joint distribution of features, citing the original Synthetic Data Vault paper. The SDV project's Gaussian Copula approach is discussed only in background prose as motivation for synthetic data augmentation, not run or evaluated in the actual experiments.

paper-performance-guaranteed-poisoning-a.summary: This paper proposes MediTab, a framework that uses large language models to consolidate, enrich, and refine heterogeneous medical tabular datasets so a single predictor can generalize across varying schemas for patient outcome and clinical trial outcome prediction. For one set of oncology clinical trial datasets with distinct schemas, the authors trained a CTGAN model on the raw data to generate synthetic patient data used in their experiments. CTGAN is run as the generator producing synthetic patient records for one of the experimental data sources.

paper-processgan-generating-privacy-pres.summary: This paper introduces ProcessGAN, a GAN-based framework using a transformer generator and a time-aware self-attention discriminator to synthesize privacy-preserving process-mining event logs, including activity sequences, timestamps, and associated patient contexts, evaluated on five real-world (including medical) datasets. The work situates itself against prior generative approaches for structured data, noting that other methods generate tabular data but lack sequential information. CTGAN is cited only as one such prior tabular-data generator in the related-work discussion, not run or compared experimentally.

paper-qacdes-qos-aware-context-2024.summary: This paper proposes QACDes, a framework for defining and validating Quality of Service (QoS) for cyber-physical systems as a function of contextual factors, enabling design-time validation before a system is fully built. It demonstrates the approach on a lighting control system case study, comparing proposed models against baselines using GAN-based data augmentation. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a reference list alongside a GAN description, with no SDV-family term appearing anywhere in the body text.

paper-synthesizing-accurate-relational-d.summary: This paper introduces MARE, a differentially private relational data synthesis algorithm designed to preserve inter-table and inter-row correlations (parent-child, sequential, associative) in structurally complex data such as electronic health records, where existing methods either ignore correlations or suffer a dimensionality explosion. The authors validate MARE on MIMIC-IV-derived and private hospital datasets, showing it retains semantically valid patient trajectories with strong privacy guarantees. In their related-work discussion they describe SDV's HMA1 algorithm as a copula-based hierarchical synthesizer that, like PrivLava, fails to model intra-table (sequential) correlations, positioning it as prior art their method improves on rather than a baseline they run.

paper-umap-partially-synthetic-healthcar.summary: This paper proposes a UMAP-based methodology for generating partially synthetic tabular healthcare data, reducing dimensionality of a reference dataset to synthesize and validate values for incomplete records, validated on prostate and breast cancer datasets and shown to outperform state-of-the-art imputation techniques. CTGAN is mentioned only in the related-work discussion of GAN-based tabular synthesis methods, without being run or compared experimentally. SDV's CTGAN is cited only as prior art in the literature review, not used in the proposed method.

paper-gan-vae-imbalanced-2023.summary: Tests whether synthetic generators still hold up when the source data is both high-dimensional and severely imbalanced, a regime where the authors argue existing evaluations are silent. CTGAN and TVAE are the two generators evaluated, so the study is a stress test of SDV's conditional sampling and its autoencoder alternative under class skew.

paper-synthetic-dataset-danish-residenti.summary: This is a data-descriptor paper presenting a synthetic dataset of five types of Danish residential electricity prosumers, combining real consumption data, PV generation modelling, EV charging simulation (emobpy), and an energy storage system operator with a GAN-based synthesizer, validated via empirical, information-theoretic, and ML-based quality metrics. CTGAN (conditional tabular generative adversarial network) is the core generative model, trained as 12 separate instances (one per user type) to produce the entire synthetic electricity time-series dataset, with a reported hyperparameter table (embedding dimension, generator/discriminator learning rates, batch size, optimiser) matching the CTGAN constructor's parameters. SDV's CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional GAN design, is run as the sole generator underpinning the whole published dataset.

paper-improved-ctgan-processing-method-2.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity and class imbalance of disk failure records used for fault diagnosis by proposing RCTGAN, a variant of CTGAN that replaces the discriminator with a residual network and adds an auxiliary classifier combined into the training loss to better distinguish real, generated, and normal/failure samples. The authors compare synthetic data quality and downstream classifier (MLP, SVM, DT, RF) diagnostic accuracy between CTGAN and their RCTGAN on disk SMART data. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator/training-by-sampling design are explicitly described as the basis being modified, with the discriminator architecture rebuilt as a residual network to create the new RCTGAN model.

paper-combining-machine-learning-methods.summary: This conference paper addresses binary detection of shaft misalignment in rotating systems using five classical machine learning classifiers (Logistic Regression, KNN, SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest) trained on a small, imbalanced tabular dataset. To address data scarcity and class imbalance, the authors apply SMOTE-LOF oversampling followed by a Conditional Tabular GAN to generate additional synthetic samples and expand the augmented dataset used for training. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as the generator producing the synthetic minority-class data that underpins the augmentation pipeline.
paper-combining-machine-learning-methods.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly (api_user) or reimplemented (port). Marked unclear pending full-text verification.

paper-ddup-learned-db-2023.summary: Proposes DDUp, a framework that decides whether newly inserted rows are out-of-distribution by running a two-sample test on the model's own loss values, then updates the learned component by sequential self-distillation instead of retraining it from scratch. TVAE, the variational autoencoder released alongside CTGAN, is the model the framework is instantiated on for the data-generation task: it is trained, then distilled with a loss the paper defines over the encoder and decoder logits, with the teacher reusing the student's latent noise.

paper-enhancing-glucose-classification-c.summary: This study applies infrared spectroscopy combined with a generative AI model to improve classification of glucose concentrations in biomass liquefaction process streams, addressing limited experimental sample sizes in a bioenergy research context. The metadata indicates the authors cite the original TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) paper as part of their generative-AI approach, though the specific mechanism of use is not recoverable from the available evidence. TGAN's tabular generative-adversarial-network method is referenced as the generative technique underlying the paper's data-enhancement strategy.
paper-enhancing-glucose-classification-c.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was actually run to generate synthetic data or merely cited as related generative-AI work.

paper-fire-resistance-analysis-synthetic.summary: This conference paper generates synthetic fire-test data for fire-resistant reinforced concrete columns to overcome the scarcity and cost of real fire experiments, then trains XGBoost regression and classification models on real versus synthetic datasets to compare predictive performance. The authors run both CTGAN and CopulaGAN to produce 10,000 synthetic samples each, evaluate them with column-correlation-based synthetic data reports, and select CopulaGAN's output as more consistent with real data for downstream analysis. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run directly as the two competing data generators whose output drives the paper's entire empirical evaluation.
paper-fire-resistance-analysis-synthetic.needs: CopulaGAN citation [4] not shown in evidence but strongly implies SDV package usage given naming; CTGAN mis-labeled as 'Continuous Time GAN' by authors.

paper-interpretable-robust-hospital-read.summary: This paper builds an interpretable and robust machine-learning model to predict 30-day hospital readmission from Electronic Health Records, combining feature selection, class-imbalance correction, and SHAP/ALE post-hoc explanations. The authors compare oversampling and cost-sensitive learning strategies, ultimately favoring cost-sensitive learning after evaluating synthetic minority oversampling. CTGAN was run to generate synthetic minority-class observations, tuned over epochs and batch size and assessed via a PCD metric, but was discarded due to poor fidelity in capturing feature relationships.
paper-interpretable-robust-hospital-read.needs: Not explicitly stated whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent CTGAN implementation was used, though tunable epochs/batch size hyperparameters suggest the library was run directly.

paper-multi-label-tabular-synthetic-2023.summary: This conference paper proposes a hybrid, sample-free synthetic data generator for multi-label 'bundle recommendation' data (e.g., bundled cosmetics purchases), combining process-driven rules with data-driven generation to avoid needing real-world sample data. The authors validate their hybrid approach by comparing its output statistically and via downstream ML accuracy against synthetic data produced by a state-of-the-art baseline. CTGAN is run as the baseline generator, trained on a sampled test dataset to produce comparison synthetic data, with its statistical fidelity and ML efficacy benchmarked against the authors' hybrid method.
paper-multi-label-tabular-synthetic-2023.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a reimplementation, and whether conditional sampling was specifically leveraged.

paper-nonparametric-generation-synthetic.summary: This paper proposes a nonparametric method for generating synthetic tabular data using empirical copulas, aiming to better preserve complex multivariate dependency structures than existing parametric or GAN-based techniques, and validates the generated data with homogeneity tests for applications in class imbalance, deep learning generalization, and anonymization. In its related-work discussion, the paper cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper, noting that it uses Gaussian copulas to generate synthetic data in the context of relational databases. SDV's Gaussian copula approach is described in prose as related prior art, not run or benchmarked in the experiments.

paper-releasing-survey-microdata-exact-2.summary: This paper proposes an alternative to geomasking for releasing georeferenced household survey microdata: fitting a Gaussian copula model to the survey attributes and sampling synthetic records per geographic cluster, tested on 2011 Costa Rican census data with satellite-derived covariates, showing large reductions in re-identification risk while preserving utility for small-area estimation. The authors explicitly state that computations were done with the sdv package, using SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer as the core generative model underlying their whole privacy-utility experiment.

paper-review-analysis-synthetic-dataset-.summary: This is a survey paper that reviews methods and techniques for generating synthetic datasets specifically for computer vision applications, covering approaches from early low-resolution generators to modern GAN-based methods, and proposes a taxonomy of nine generation methods and 17 processes. It discusses the SDV founding paper only in a brief prose mention, citing its 2016 study finding real-data results could be reproduced with synthetic data alone in 70% of cases, without engaging further or running any SDV tool.
paper-review-analysis-synthetic-dataset-.needs: Full text not obtained; only the abstract/citing sentence is available, so it is unclear whether SDV is discussed further elsewhere in the review.

paper-sequential-poi-recommend-personali.summary: This paper proposes FedSR, a personalized federated learning framework for sequential point-of-interest (POI) recommendation, combining contrastive learning, Bayesian personalized ranking, and locality-sensitive hashing based client grouping to address data sparsity and Non-IID issues while preserving privacy. It is validated on two real-world check-in datasets. The paper's reference list cites 'Sequential models in the synthetic data vault' (PAR), but the term never appears in the body text, indicating a bibliographic-only citation.
paper-sequential-poi-recommend-personali.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata available. Cannot confirm whether the cited SDV paper (tagged 'sequential-2022') is DeepEcho/PAR or another work, nor how it is used (baseline, related work, or mere citation).

paper-synthetic-generation-enterprise-db.summary: A tutorial paper surveying three decades of synthetic database generation techniques for enterprise DBMS testing, covering ab initio generation, database-dependent regeneration, and query-workload-dependent regeneration, and closing with open research problems. It describes CTGAN's conditional generator design for modeling multimodal continuous columns and imbalanced categorical columns as one of the representative database-dependent regeneration techniques covered in detail. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator are described in prose as part of the survey, not run or benchmarked by the authors.
paper-synthetic-generation-enterprise-db.needs: The original SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) appears only in the reference list; the body's detailed CTGAN discussion is tied to a separate Xu et al. 2019 citation, so the exact linkage between the tracked sdv-dsaa-2016 citation and the body text is inferred rather than directly shown.

paper-universal-metric-robust-evaluation.summary: This paper proposes TabSynDex, a single bounded metric that combines several component scores to robustly evaluate the quality of synthetic tabular data, and uses it to reveal training-dynamics problems (e.g., CTGAN not actually learning during 300-epoch training) that existing disparate metrics miss. The authors benchmark TabSynDex against CTGAN, TGAN, TVAE, WGAN-GP and several of their own architectural variants (bidirectional TGAN, TGAN+GRU, VGMM preprocessing) across four tabular datasets. CTGAN and TVAE, the SDV-family generative synthesizers, are run with default hyperparameters as evaluation subjects whose synthetic outputs the whole comparative study rests on.
paper-universal-metric-robust-evaluation.needs: Evidence does not explicitly confirm the sdv-dev CTGAN/TVAE package was imported (no constructor parameter names or import statements shown); could alternatively be an authors' reimplementation given the architectural modifications applied to TGAN variants.

paper-deformablegan-generating-medical-i.summary: This paper studies checkerboard artifacts produced during adversarial training in GAN-based medical image synthesis and proposes a deformable-convolution-based method to eliminate them while preserving image integrity for healthcare cyber-physical systems. It evaluates the method across several GAN architectures used for medical image reconstruction, segmentation, and synthesis, and also shows the artifacts can be used to detect GAN-generated images. CTGAN is cited only in passing, alongside an unrelated conditional-GAN image-captioning paper, as prior art for 'conditional GAN structure' with no tabular-synthesis engagement.
paper-deformablegan-generating-medical-i.needs: Affiliations for authors other than Zhangyi Shen are not visible in the truncated first-page evidence.

paper-efficient-bayesian-network-constru.summary: This paper improves DataSynthesizer's Bayesian-network-based synthetic data generation by replacing its greedy structure-learning algorithm with a faster genetic algorithm, aiming to improve efficiency on high-dimensional datasets while also reducing attribute disclosure risk through targeted correlation suppression. The Synthetic Data Vault is mentioned only in passing as an alternative synthesizer for datasets with hundreds to thousands of attributes, never run or evaluated.
paper-efficient-bayesian-network-constru.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so any deeper engagement with SDV beyond this passing mention cannot be ruled out.

paper-comparison-machine-learning-method.summary: This conference paper compares Random Forest, AutoML methods, and a deep Autoencoder against five class-balancing strategies for extremely unbalanced industrial quality datasets from a major automotive assembly manufacturer, finding Random Forest combined with Gaussian Copula oversampling gave competitive results. The Gaussian Copula balancing technique was implemented using the sdv library, run as one of several oversampling strategies (alongside SMOTE, Random Undersampling, and Tomek Links) rather than a novel contribution of the paper. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is used as an oversampling generator, run alongside SMOTE and other balancing methods to address extreme class imbalance in industrial quality prediction.
paper-comparison-machine-learning-method.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations and deeper methodological detail on how GC was applied could not be verified beyond the abstract and cited sentences.

paper-crowdteacher-robust-teaching-noisy.summary: This paper proposes CrowdTeacher, a co-teaching framework for classification with noisy crowdsourced labels on tabular data, which perturbs samples by an amount proportional to their label uncertainty using synthetic data drawn from a fitted data synthesizer. The authors experimentally compare three synthesizers -- CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian copula -- for generating the perturbation samples feeding CrowdTeacher, finding Gaussian copula gives the largest performance gain and adopting it for the remaining experiments. CTGAN, TVAE, and the Gaussian copula synthesizer from the Synthetic Data Vault family are each run directly as interchangeable data-generation components within the proposed pipeline, with Gaussian copula selected as the final synthesizer used throughout the study.
paper-crowdteacher-robust-teaching-noisy.needs: Evidence does not specify whether the SDV library package or the authors' own implementation was used to run CTGAN/TVAE/Gaussian copula; treated as api_user given direct experimental use and named synthesizer citations.

paper-increasing-prediction-accuracy-pat.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based sample-augmentation pipeline for cancer stage prediction from DNA mutation and RNA expression data, selecting significant genes via random forest feature ranking before expanding RNA expression data with a custom GAN and classifying stage with random forest, DNNs, and 1D-CNNs. The authors report large F1 gains from augmented datasets on several TCGA cancer types. TGAN is mentioned only in the related-work discussion, described as applying LSTM with attention to generate column-by-column tabular data, but it is not implemented or run in the study.
paper-increasing-prediction-accuracy-pat.needs: TGAN is only described in related work as prior art on tabular GANs; the authors' own augmentation GAN is a separate, unnamed architecture and TGAN code is not run.

paper-mtcopula-synthetic-complex-generat.summary: This conference paper proposes MTCopula, a new copula-based method for generating synthetic complex/mixed-type data, motivated by the observation that most prior copula-based synthetic data approaches rely solely on the Gaussian copula paired with Pearson correlation. It positions itself as departing from this limitation by modeling dependencies and marginal behaviors more flexibly. The original SDV paper is cited as one of the prior contributions exemplifying this Gaussian-copula-only approach that the authors' method improves upon.
paper-mtcopula-synthetic-complex-generat.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so it is unclear whether SDV's code/library was ever run or only its Gaussian Copula approach discussed.

paper-baseline-attribute-disclosure-risk.summary: This paper reformulates attribute disclosure risk assessment in synthetic data as a machine learning classification problem, comparing existing disclosure risk measures to classifier-based reformulations, and proposes improved baseline attacks using RadiusNearestNeighbor and EnsembleVote classifiers. The authors empirically evaluate attribute disclosure risk and utility trade-offs across synthetic datasets generated by multiple tools. SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer is run as one of three synthetic data generators (alongside DataSynthesizer and synthpop) whose outputs are subjected to the paper's disclosure-risk attacks.
paper-baseline-attribute-disclosure-risk.needs: Only abstract and citing sentence available; full text not obtained, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body beyond this pointer citation.

paper-synergistic-deep-learning-knowledg.summary: This conference paper proposes a hybrid framework combining knowledge engineering with deep learning, arguing that neither approach alone adequately captures the structure of complex problem domains. It surveys challenges of modern deep learning, including its dependence on large training datasets, and notes synthetic-data generation as one response to data scarcity. The SDV-family vine copula paper (Sun, Cuesta-Infante, and Veeramachaneni 2019) is cited only as an example of such synthetic-data-generation research, with no method run.
paper-synergistic-deep-learning-knowledg.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so cannot confirm whether the vine copula work is discussed further beyond this single passing mention.

paper-generating-high-fidelity-synthetic.summary: This paper presents a method for generating synthetic UK primary-care patient data by integrating resampling, probabilistic graphical modelling, latent variable identification, and outlier analysis, aiming to preserve feature distributions, dependencies, and ML sensitivity-analysis statistics while quantifying re-identification risk. It is published in npj Digital Medicine. The Synthetic Data Vault is mentioned only once in a single sentence listing prior generative-model approaches to synthetic data, with the SDV paper cited as reference 11 and no further engagement or use.
paper-generating-high-fidelity-synthetic.needs: None — full text confirms citation is bibliographic only, with no SDV usage or description beyond the single passing sentence.

paper-ctgan-2019.summary: Introduces CTGAN and TVAE, together with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling to handle imbalanced categorical columns and multi-modal continuous columns. The most cited artifact in the ecosystem and the standard baseline for tabular synthesis.

paper-virtual-patient-model-generating-2.summary: This paper proposes the Virtual Patient Model (VPM), a system combining a genetic algorithm, statistical analysis, and machine learning to generate synthetic healthcare time-series data that preserves statistical similarity to real patient data while retaining differences useful for training predictive models. It validates VPM on real-world time-series datasets using statistical tests and comparative machine-learning classification performance. The paper cites the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper as prior work that synthesizes discrete relational data by sampling from a learned statistical distribution, contrasting it with VPM's time-series approach, but does not run SDV itself.
paper-virtual-patient-model-generating-2.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body beyond related-work framing.

paper-exploring-optimal-granularity-mark.summary: This paper investigates how to determine an optimal level of market segmentation granularity in real-time bidding (RTB) online advertising using a computational/agent-based experimental approach. It builds simulation models to test segmentation strategies and their effect on advertising market outcomes. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper, apparently in connection with generating or referencing synthetic datasets for its computational experiments.
paper-exploring-optimal-granularity-mark.needs: No abstract or full text was available; only the citation link to the SDV 2016 paper is known, so the actual role of SDV in this work cannot be verified beyond a bare citation.

preprint-filtered-mixture-generators-ful.summary: This paper proposes FoGS, a two-level pipeline for fully synthetic survival-analysis training that reframes synthetic-data construction as sample selection rather than generation: a pool of four architecturally distinct generators produces candidates, an ensemble of survival models scores per-sample plausibility, and an outer loop tunes a selection policy against held-out downstream performance on 16 public clinical datasets. One of the four candidate generators, SurvivalCTGAN, adapts CTGAN's GAN component with a survival head (following SurvivalGAN methodology) to model censored time-to-event data alongside covariates. CTGAN's generator architecture is thus modified into a new named variant and run as one of four generators feeding the FoGS candidate pool, evaluated (and found to underperform alone) against the filtered mixture.
preprint-filtered-mixture-generators-ful.needs: Unclear whether SurvivalCTGAN's implementation reuses sdv-dev CTGAN code directly or is an independent reimplementation of the CTGAN architecture; treated as derivative_work per the architecture-modification rule.

preprint-declarative-outcome-conformant-.summary: This preprint proposes 'outcome-conformant synthesis' — a closed-form, deterministic method for generating relational tabular data that exactly satisfies declared analytical outcomes (aggregates, rates, group shares) with no source data, contrasting this 'conformance' axis with the fidelity axis on which imitation methods are judged. It introduces SpecBench, a benchmark measuring conformance for cold-start relational synthesis, and a reference implementation compared against several baselines. SDV's GaussianCopula, CTGAN, and HMA synthesizers are run as-is (via the installed sdv package, version 1.37.0) as imitation/relational baseline comparators across multiple experiments, consistently shown to fail exact-aggregate conformance even in a per-period-conditioned steelman variant.

preprint-off-policy-evaluation-strategic.summary: This paper studies off-policy evaluation (OPE) under strategic behavior, where decision subjects modify their covariates in response to a policy, inducing a policy-dependent covariate shift. The authors propose a local information disclosure mechanism using post-hoc explanations, model agents' cost sensitivity via a conditional log-normal distribution, and construct a doubly robust estimator for policy value, validated on the German Credit dataset. CTGAN is run to generate 200,000 additional synthetic samples used to expand the experimental dataset for their strategic-agent simulation.

paper-tabgraa-post-training-2026.summary: Treats a tabular language model as something to keep improving after supervised fine-tuning, running a generate-score-align loop in which sampled rows are ranked by a task-specified reward and the model is updated against a frozen reference, with TabGRAA comparing high- and low-reward groups by group-averaged log-ratios instead of paired preferences. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines run from their official codebases, and the classifier two-sample test that scores indistinguishability is SDMetrics' C2ST quality score.

preprint-seq2synth-benchmarking-temporal.summary: This paper introduces Seq2Synth, a taxonomy-guided benchmark for evaluating whether synthetic sequential tabular data preserve temporal structure, testing timestamp validity, cross-sectional dynamics, longitudinal trajectories, and relational structure across 13 datasets and eight generators. The authors show that models scoring well on conventional static-distribution metrics can still produce invalid timestamps or distorted trajectories, revealing that temporal fidelity cannot be inferred from static or relational metrics alone. SDV, cited to the original 2016 Synthetic Data Vault paper, is run as one of eight relational/sequential synthesizers evaluated throughout the benchmark's extensive result tables, its relational (HMA-style) synthesis serving as one evaluation subject among several rather than the paper's own proposed method.
preprint-seq2synth-benchmarking-temporal.needs: Whether 'SDV' denotes the sdv-dev HMASynthesizer package run directly or a reimplementation is not stated explicitly in the visible text; treated as api_user given the citation to the original SDV paper and no described reimplementation.

paper-tabdlm-2026.summary: Handles tables whose columns mix numbers with free-form text such as reviews or clinical notes by running a joint diffusion process over a continuous numerical latent and a discrete language latent, so text fields are generated in step with the structured columns rather than as an afterthought. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN-based and VAE-based baselines it is measured against, and the Shape and Trend fidelity scores it reports are the SDMetrics column-shape and column-pair-trend metrics.

preprint-power-order-fooling-llms-2026.summary: This paper introduces Adversarial Table Permutation (ATP), a gradient-based attack that finds worst-case semantically-invariant row/column permutations of tabular inputs to degrade LLM performance on table question answering, revealing that modern LLMs are not robust to table layout despite the data's underlying permutation invariance. In a related-work paragraph on synthetic tabular data generation, the paper briefly describes CTGAN's conditional GAN approach with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling as prior art, without running or evaluating it.

preprint-quantitative-comparison-structu.summary: This medRxiv preprint quantitatively evaluates the structural and distributional fidelity of a synthetic tabular dataset (N=500) modeling Parkinson's disease patients against a real clinical dataset (N=57), using correlation-matrix stability, PCA variance capture, and Jensen-Shannon distance as fidelity metrics. It finds that univariate distributional similarity does not guarantee preservation of multivariate correlation structure, especially for clinical scales like UPDRS. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited repeatedly as background for general concepts of synthetic data fidelity evaluation and privacy-preserving data sharing, and CTGAN is named only in passing as one example of a tabular-data GAN variant, with neither library actually run in the study.
preprint-quantitative-comparison-structu.needs: Neither SDV nor CTGAN is described as the actual generator used to produce the study's synthetic dataset; the generation method itself is not clearly specified in the available evidence.

paper-low-flammability-polymers-platform.summary: Predicts flammability metrics for polymers, where measurement is expensive and the experimental set is correspondingly small, comparing hand-built polymer descriptors against RDKit-generated ones across an ML sweep. SDV is run to synthesise extra polymers and enlarge the experimental dataset before that sweep — one augmentation step feeding a broader descriptor study rather than the study's subject.
paper-low-flammability-polymers-platform.needs: no arXiv HTML rendering exists for this submission; confirm from the PDF which synthesizer was used and whether the augmentation changed the reported metrics.

preprint-differentially-private-linear-r.summary: This paper proposes a unified method for linear regression and synthetic data generation under Gaussian differential privacy, providing a bias-corrected estimator with valid asymptotic confidence intervals and a synthetic-data procedure whose downstream regression matches the DP linear regression results. It targets small- to medium-scale social-science datasets, where existing deep-learning-based DP synthesizers are shown to be less reliable. In experiments, DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN -- DP-enhanced variants of CTGAN implemented via the SmartNoise library -- are used as baseline comparators, with CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) cited as their origin rather than run directly through SDV.
preprint-differentially-private-linear-r.needs: DP-CTGAN/PATE-CTGAN are run extensively as baselines via SmartNoise, not the SDV package; CTGAN itself is only cited as the originating paper, so treated as citation_only per the descendant rule.

preprint-risk-context-benchmarking-priva.summary: This paper benchmarks three in-context-learning foundation-model tabular generators (GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 3.3 70B, TabPFN v2) against four data-specific baselines across 35 real-world health, finance, and policy tables, measuring statistical fidelity, downstream ML utility, and membership-inference privacy leakage. It finds foundation models occupy the riskiest end of the privacy spectrum while CTGAN offers a favorable quality-leakage tradeoff, and it uses SDMetrics' implementation for its fidelity metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of the four deep-learning baselines the foundation models are benchmarked against, and SDMetrics is used to implement the fidelity evaluation.

preprint-high-supervised-learning-utilit.summary: This paper proposes PRRO, a data-centric pipeline that combines data pruning and column reordering to improve the downstream supervised-learning utility of synthetic tabular data, evaluated on 22 public datasets. It targets class-imbalance exaggeration and overlooked inter-column relationships in existing tabular generators rather than proposing a new generator itself. SDV and CTGAN are cited only in passing, as bibliographic examples of generators that model whole-table cross-feature relationships, with no library code run.

preprint-density-ratio-framework-evaluat.summary: This paper proposes a density ratio estimation framework to evaluate the utility of synthetic data, developing global and local utility measures that improve on established procedures, and provides an accompanying open-source R package, densityratio. It is a methods paper focused on synthetic data quality evaluation broadly, not tied to any specific generator. CTGAN is only mentioned once in passing, as an example of a complex deep-learning-based synthesis method, and is cited only in the reference list.

preprint-augmented-surprise-guided-seque.summary: This preprint proposes SurpriseAF-BO, a surprise-guided sequential Bayesian optimization framework for predicting melt pool depth, width, and length in metal additive manufacturing from limited process data. The authors then extend it into CT-SurpriseAF-BO by augmenting the small training set with synthetic samples, improving prediction RMSE without additional physical experiments. CTGAN is run as the synthetic data generator underpinning this augmentation, with a reported hyperparameter table (embedding dim, generator dim, discriminator dim, generator/discriminator lr) matching the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation.

preprint-ctg-krew-generating-synthetic-2.summary: This paper proposes CTG-KrEW, a framework that combines K-Means clustering and word embeddings with Conditional Tabular GAN to generate synthetic tabular data whose categorical attributes (e.g., freelancer skillsets) retain semantic and contextual coherence, evaluated on an Upwork freelancing dataset against generic CTGAN and a multi-hot-encoded CTGAN baseline. The proposed encoding scheme is fed into CTGAN to reduce redundant category combinations and improve variability, similarity, and resource efficiency over standard one-hot encoding. CTGAN is run via the open-source SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) library as the generative core for all three compared variants, with the authors' clustering-based preprocessing layered on top of the unmodified SDV implementation.
preprint-ctg-krew-generating-synthetic-2.needs: Whether the authors' clustering/multi-hot encoding preprocessing counts as modifying CTGAN itself or is purely an external preprocessing step feeding the unmodified SDV CTGAN synthesizer; treated here as api_user since the generator itself (SDV's CTGAN class, per pseudocode 'CTGAN synthesizer.fit/save/load/sample') runs unmodified.

paper-dsf-gan-feedback-2024.summary: Adds a downstream feedback loop to tabular GAN training: a predictor trained on the real data scores each batch of generated rows and its loss is folded into the generator objective, so the generator is pushed toward samples that are useful for the eventual task rather than only plausible. CTGAN is the base architecture the mechanism is built on and demonstrated with, its generator loss rewritten to carry the extra feedback term, and the experiments use that architecture throughout.

preprint-plagiarism-index-characterizing.summary: This paper introduces the Data Plagiarism Index (DPI), a new similarity metric and Membership Inference Attack designed to detect and quantify data-copying in tabular generative models, arguing existing methods either ignore privacy threat framing or fail to scale to high-dimensional mixed-type tabular data. The authors benchmark DPI's MIA against other attacks across a wide range of tabular generators (CTGAN, TVAE, Normalizing Flows, Bayesian Network, ARF, Tab-DDPM, PATEGAN, Ads-GAN) using implementations drawn from the Synthcity package, showing that CTGAN and other common architectures exhibit data-copying that poses privacy and fairness risks. CTGAN and TVAE, cited to the original CTGAN paper, are run as two of several benchmarked generator architectures via a third-party library rather than the SDV package itself.
preprint-plagiarism-index-characterizing.needs: CTGAN/TVAE were run via the Synthcity package's implementations rather than the sdv-dev package directly, so it is unclear whether Synthcity's code is itself derived from SDV or an independent reimplementation.

paper-smart-vehicle-information-leakage-.summary: Argues that connected-vehicle telemetry leaks more about the driver than the service needs, and tests synthetic data as the mitigation, evaluating the result on fidelity, utility and privacy in turn. TVAE from SDV is chosen after trying the library's other models, and fidelity is scored with SDV's own evaluation metrics, so both the generation and its acceptance criteria come from running the library.

preprint-improving-trip-mode-choice-2024.summary: This preprint proposes ENSY, a probability-distribution-based data augmentation method designed to improve classification accuracy for minority classes in travel mode-choice datasets, and evaluates it against Random Oversampling, SMOTE-NC, and CTGAN on the LPMC and KTDB datasets. ENSY is shown to substantially raise minority-class F1 scores and overall accuracy relative to these baselines. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN originally described in the SDV-family paper, is run as one of the comparison baselines, with the authors explicitly noting that SDV (and YData) offer packaged CTGAN implementations but that they instead used a separate open-source version for finer control.
preprint-improving-trip-mode-choice-2024.needs: Unclear whether the 'open-source version' of CTGAN used is the sdv-dev/CTGAN package itself or an independent reimplementation; paper explicitly contrasts its choice with the SDV package.

preprint-plasmode-simulation-evaluation-.summary: This paper develops a statistical framework for generating replicated plasmode simulation datasets from private, homophilous social network data, using an exponential family random graph model fitted to the network combined with resampling from observed exposure/covariate distributions to preserve associations. In surveying prior approaches to synthetic data generation, the authors describe the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as a Python tool that estimates the joint distribution of a population via a latent Gaussian copula, but they instead implement their own covariate/exposure generation using the R package GenOrd. SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer is discussed as related work, not run.

preprint-designing-user-centric-behavior.summary: This paper proposes ExAct, a model-agnostic framework for generating counterfactual explanations that suggest actionable behavioral interventions to prevent adverse health events such as blood glucose spikes, evaluated on four real-world health datasets. To supplement a small nutrition-absorption dataset, the authors describe using a conditional autoregressive model to generate synthetic glycemic response data given new context. SDV's sequential PAR model is run as the augmentation tool producing synthetic training data for one of the four datasets used in the evaluation.
preprint-designing-user-centric-behavior.needs: Evidence conflicts: the passage describing SDV's PAR model use appears to be from an appendix/rebuttal Q&A, while an accompanying note claims no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list. paper-calime-causal-lime-2022.summary: Attacks the feature-independence assumption in local post-hoc explanation by learning a causal graph over the data first and sampling the local neighbourhood along it, so that the perturbed instances LIME queries the black box with respect the dependencies present in the real data. SDV supplies the statistical machinery for judging that neighbourhood: the paper adopts its Gaussian mixture log-likelihood, inverted Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and its binned approximation of continuous KL divergence to compare generated instances against the real distribution, and notes that a prior method used CTGAN for the same neighbourhood-realism purpose.

preprint-stasy-score-tabular-synthesis-2.summary: This paper proposes STaSy, a score-based generative model for synthetic tabular data that incorporates a self-paced learning strategy and a fine-tuning step to stabilize denoising score matching training. It benchmarks against seven baselines including CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, OCT-GAN, MedGAN, VEEGAN, and RNODE across 15 datasets on sampling quality, diversity, and runtime, and cites Patki et al. (2016)'s recursive Gaussian-copula table modeling as prior work on tabular synthesis. CTGAN and TVAE are run as baseline synthesizers via the SDGym package (github.com/sdv-dev/SDGym), while SDV's original Gaussian copula approach is only cited as related work.

preprint-cidatgan-conditional-inputs-tab.summary: This technical report proposes ciDATGAN, an evolution of the authors' own Directed Acyclic Tabular GAN (DATGAN) that adds conditional inputs inspired by image-completion methods, and shows it can be used to debias datasets and complete large synthetic populations from a smaller feeder dataset. In its related-work discussion of tabular GANs, the paper describes CTGAN's introduction of conditionality via concatenation and notes it demonstrates the conditional vector is critical for imbalanced datasets, without providing specific conditionality results itself. CTGAN's conditional vector is discussed as prior art the authors' own DATGAN-based model departs from, but CTGAN is never run in the experiments.

preprint-privgen-preserving-privacy-sequ.summary: This preprint proposes PrivGen, a method for generating synthetic sequential data that preserves patterns and characteristics of source data (e.g., GPS trajectories, medical event sequences) while limiting privacy risk, evaluated against real-world datasets to show the generated data preserves the sequential model trained on the original. It is positioned within the broader field of privacy-preserving data publication and generation methods, citing prior anonymization and synthetic data approaches. The original SDV paper is only cited in the reference list as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no use of the SDV library or its methods in the paper's own approach.

thesis-automatically-linking-elements-20.summary: An MIT M.Eng. thesis proposing ADEL, a system that automatically generates metadata annotations (schemas, field types, relationships) for relational datasets, then feeds those annotations into downstream data-science automation tools. The thesis uses Deep Feature Synthesis and the Synthetic Data Vault as two endpoint systems to evaluate whether automatically inferred annotations can substitute for manually specified ones. The Synthetic Data Vault's hierarchical relational synthesizer is run as one of the two evaluation endpoints, generating synthetic multi-table data from ADEL's automatically produced schema and being checked for constraint violations.
